verdict.rationale: Blocking tracking pixels and being transparent about mail-data use are fair questions for an email client like Outlook, so the axis applies. However, the evidence pack contains nothing on remote-image or tracking-pixel blocking, default privacy protections, or data-use transparency. The cited material covers Graph mail APIs, link handling, performance and ads on free accounts, none of which addresses this story.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data
